title: Where it started
body: Born and bred in Cantù, near Lake Como. I started skateboarding in 2007, and in 2012 a nollie flip ran in 6:00am magazine, my first photo in print. From 2014 I helped friends build a concrete skatepark in town.

photos.alt: Nollie flip in a dark underpass, against the light from the stairs behind
photos.caption: Nollie flip, 6:00am, 2012

photos.alt: Skating a quarter pipe at the concrete park in Cantù, reflected in a puddle
photos.caption: The skatepark we built

photos.alt: Ollie off a concrete barrier under a motorway bridge

title: More skateboarding and trips around Europe
body: Italian brand FVTVRA put me on their board team. That meant small skate trips around Italy, Slovenia and Spain, filming and shooting photos wherever we found a spot.

photos.alt: Skating the ledges at the Blast! The Big One contest in front of a crowd
Fisheye shot of a kickflip at a skatepark under a flyover
Magazine page with a gap to frontside smith grind on a ledge in L’Aquila
photos.caption: Gap to frontside smith, L’Aquila, 2016

photos.alt: FVTVRA magazine ad: a pole jam across a bent bollard on the left page, three TWIM IV board graphics on the right
photos.caption: FVTVRA TWIM IV ad, 2017

photos.alt: Backside tailslide down a concrete pyramid in Málaga
photos.caption: Backside tailslide

title: First job: skate teacher
body: For three summers I taught skateboarding at Gattarella Resort on the Gargano coast. My students were resort guests of every age, from small kids to their parents.

photos.alt: Two of us on the rocks at Gattarella at sunset, looking out to the islands

title: Brighton, behind the bar
body: In January 2019 I moved to Brighton, took a bartending course and started working at the Hilton. That year I made the final of Hilton's UK & Ireland cocktail competition, with a finger I'd broken skating in London.

photos.alt: Holding a certificate on stage at the Flavour & Flair final with three Hilton hosts
photos.caption: Flavour & Flair, Hilton UK & Ireland final, 2019

photos.alt: Straining two pink cocktails into coupes at the bar

title: First app: Drinko
body: Since getting that MacBook Pro, I'd been teaching myself Xcode through YouTube, e-books and courses. During the pandemic it finally clicked, and I built Drinko, a cocktail app that put the bar handbook in my colleagues' pockets.

photos.alt: Drinko app icon
Photographing a mojito against a white backdrop

title: Cocktails to go
body: Covid sent me home, and I started at a new bar. Then lockdown shut that too, so it was time to sell frozen cocktails and deliver them ourselves. The wrestling mask was optional.

photos.alt: In a luchador mask behind the bar, holding up two bags of frozen cocktails

title: Back to Brighton: head bartender
body: A few months later the Hilton called me back to Brighton, this time as head bartender. I created my own drinks there, down to the homemade spiced pineapple bitters in the photo.

photos.alt: Pouring a clear drink into a coupe with a crisp garnish
A clear cocktail in a coupe with a crisp garnish, on a marble table
Handing over a short drink topped with foam

title: Making my own gin
body: In 2022 I became the hotel's Monkey 47 ambassador, which took me to the distillery in the Black Forest. I stirred a barrel of botanicals with a power drill and went home with a bottle of gin I'd made myself.

photos.alt: Holding my own bottle of gin in its box at the Monkey 47 distillery

title: One tweet
body: I was a head bartender when a tweet changed my life. One DM, a CV and a few interviews later, I swapped the bar for SwiftUI.

photos.alt: Tweet from @tundsdev: Soooo My workplace is currently looking 3 iOS devs 👀 Specifically 1 Junior & 2 mids. We’re based in Manchester UK & have a 3 day a week office policy We’re working on a fully SwiftUI app for a brand new project. If you’re interested in the role drop me a DM 🤝 Any RT & shares would be greatly appreciated 🫂

title: Freelancing on the side
body: Alongside my day job I started freelancing, building a macOS app for a Brighton company. It helps them process music royalty and revenue reports. Today I'm an iOS engineer with four apps shipped.

title: Running 22 km
body: On 4 October 2026 I ran 22 km around Manchester in 2h 15m. I’d prepped for a few months, and it was still a tough run, but worth the effort.

photos.alt: Strava summary over a selfie: 22.01 km, 6:08 per km, 2h 15m, 217 m elevation gain, 164 bpm average heart rate.
